description: Dimensions of a media present. A configuration assigns exactly one value per dimension. 'ground' is our world's value. k = the number of dimensions whose sampled value differs from ground (Hamming distance from the all-ground configuration). This is the compile-time artifact for world generation. Each value also carries a 'worldFact' — the plain-language sentence the renderer must honor for that value (via the worldFacts map); the changed moves' worldFacts become the World object's facts list.

conventions.exclusive: true = the named value strictly holds and its alternatives do not. false = EMPHASIS: the value names what predominates or is especially important in this world, not an absolute exclusion — other modes may persist in the background.
conventions.ordered: false for every dimension except 'resemblance', whose values form a natural progression (kept as metadata; sampling treats it like any nominal set).
conventions.groundGloss: optional qualifier on the ground value carrying stance/detail not reducible to the bare value id.
conventions.glosses: short designer-facing descriptions for non-obvious / merged / renamed values.
conventions.worldFacts: render-facing plain sentences, one per value, with NO dimension vocabulary. A world's changed (off-ground) values are translated through this map into the World's facts list. Emphasis values say 'predominantly/mostly'; exclusive values state flatly.

changelog: v3 (2026-07-17): added worldFacts (value→plain sentence) for the unified world model. v2: culled to 9 dimensions (dropped fidelity_criterion, address), merges/renames, added exclusive flag; sensory values renamed to *-primary.

dimensions.label: Attention unit
dimensions.description: the social size at which media is attended to

glosses.congregation: associational — social clubs, political parties, collective bodies

worldFacts.solitary: Media is attended to alone, one person at a time.
worldFacts.congregation: Media is attended to in gathered groups — clubs, halls, congregations — rather than alone.

dimensions.label: Sensory register
dimensions.description: the sensory channel media primarily works through

glosses.visual-primary: predominantly visual — image leads; sound recedes but is not absent
glosses.auditory-primary: predominantly auditory — sound leads; image recedes but is not absent
glosses.haptic-proprioceptive-primary: touch and bodily position/movement brought forward as the leading channel (merged haptic + proprioceptive)

worldFacts.audiovisual: Media works through combined sound and image.
worldFacts.visual-primary: Media works predominantly through the image; sound recedes but is not absent.
worldFacts.auditory-primary: Media works predominantly through sound; the image recedes but is not absent.
worldFacts.haptic-proprioceptive-primary: The media that matter most are experienced through the body — touch, motion, and balance — more than by watching or listening.

dimensions.label: Resemblance
dimensions.description: how closely media imagery aims to look like its subject
dimensions.groundGloss: aspiring (our world sits at photorealist and reaches upward)

worldFacts.abstract: Media imagery is abstract, making no attempt to resemble its subject.
worldFacts.cartoon: Media imagery is cartoon-like — simplified and stylized rather than lifelike.
worldFacts.realist: Media imagery aims to look convincingly real.
worldFacts.photorealist: Media imagery aims for photographic realism.
worldFacts.hyperreal: Media imagery is hyperreal — sharper and more vivid than lived perception.

dimensions.label: Authorship distribution
dimensions.description: who is entitled to make media

glosses.caste-hereditary: authorship by birth, lineage, or caste (wild option)

worldFacts.professional: Media is made by a professional class of makers.
worldFacts.universal: Everyone makes media; there is no separate class of professional makers.
worldFacts.algorithmic: Media is produced by machines and models rather than by people.
worldFacts.caste-hereditary: The right to make media is inherited, restricted to a hereditary caste.

dimensions.label: Provisioning
dimensions.description: the economic relation by which media is funded or obtained
dimensions.groundGloss: advertising, purchase, and subscription — the capitalist default (merged)

worldFacts.commercial-market: Media is paid for through the market — bought, subscribed to, or funded by advertising.
worldFacts.welfare-entitlement: Access to media is a publicly guaranteed right, not something bought.
worldFacts.civic-duty: Media is provided and supported as a public obligation.
worldFacts.gift-reciprocal: Media circulates mostly as gift and mutual exchange rather than for money.
worldFacts.patronage: Media is supported mainly by patrons who commission and sustain it.

dimensions.label: Custody
dimensions.description: where media resides and how long it persists

glosses.in-body-mortal: resides in the body and dies with the person

worldFacts.remote-tenancy: People rent access to media held on remote platforms, which can revoke it at will.
worldFacts.personal-possession: People own their media outright — held, kept, resold, and inherited.
worldFacts.civic-archive: Media is held in public archives that everyone can draw on.
worldFacts.in-body-mortal: People carry their media inside their own bodies; it dies with them and cannot be copied out.

dimensions.label: Literacy floor
dimensions.description: the assumed minimum competence of a media participant; higher competences subsume lower

glosses.world-build: able to construct environments or worlds
glosses.model-train: able to train or steer models

worldFacts.read+type: The assumed baseline skill for taking part in media is reading and typing.
worldFacts.none: No skill is assumed; media requires no literacy to take part.
worldFacts.read-only: People are assumed to read media but not to produce it.
worldFacts.world-build: The assumed baseline skill is building whole environments or worlds.
worldFacts.model-train: The assumed baseline skill is training and steering generative models, the way we assume reading.
worldFacts.perform-from-memory: The assumed baseline skill is performing works from memory.

dimensions.label: Compulsion
dimensions.description: how obligatory participation in media is
dimensions.groundGloss: optional in name, compulsory in fact

glosses.forbidden-by-class: participation gated by economic or social class (merged forbidden-to-some + forbidden-to-most)

worldFacts.optional-but-compulsory-in-fact: Taking part in media is optional in name but unavoidable in practice.
worldFacts.freely-optional: Taking part in media is genuinely optional.
worldFacts.compulsory-by-law: Taking part in media is required by law.
worldFacts.initiatory: Taking part in media is gained through rite or initiation.
worldFacts.forbidden-by-class: Taking part in media is restricted by class — permitted to some, forbidden to others.

dimensions.label: Metering
dimensions.description: the unit by which media use is counted or charged

worldFacts.attention-metered-and-sold: People's attention is measured and sold to advertisers.
worldFacts.unmetered: Media use is not counted or charged at all.
worldFacts.quota-per-person: Each person receives a fixed ration of media.
